_readme: calc_cases.json v1 — the specification of Budget X's arithmetic (Round 03, Builder C).
Run with: node tools/calc_golden.mjs   (exits non-zero on any mismatch).
Every expectation here is an INTEGER CENT value or a formatted string. Nothing in this
file is a rand float, and nothing anywhere multiplies by 100 — the stored column already
holds cents (spec_03 §0.1).
Arg resolvers understood by the runner:
{"$ref": "fixture"}                       the fixture array/object itself
{"$index": "fixture"}                     bxSmartIndex(fixture)
{"$call": {"fn": "...", "args": [...]}}    a composed call, resolved recursively
Case options: "pluck": "transaction_id" compares selected ids instead of whole rows;
"throws": "substring" expects a throw; "legacy_compare" additionally runs the ported
legacy is_it_smart and REQUIRES its answer to differ (spec_03 AC-5.5).
The transfer sentinel category id is ec8e0085-8408-43a2-953f-ebba24549d96 (spec_03 §3.2).
v2 (Round 04, Builder C) adds the cases for spec_04 §3.3's sixteen new exports.
Every expectation below is HAND-COMPUTED from §4.5 (rollover), §4.5A (the month
pool) and §4.6 (the progress meter) — never recorded from a run of bx_calc.js.
Fixtures are deliberately small and use round cent values so any figure here can
be re-derived with mental arithmetic from the fixture rows.
Two further case options the v2 runner understands:
"legacy_rollover": {...}   also runs the ported legacy BUDGET.py roll_over_calc
on the same fixtures and REQUIRES its answer to equal
the month's own actual (variance 0, "exactly on
budget") while bxRollover reports overspent > 0 and
remaining == 0 — spec_04 AC-5.5, fact 12.
{"$sort": {"fn": ..., "of": ...}}  sorts an array THROUGH an exported
comparator, which is the only way to show bxCompare
is a total order (§3.11 carry-fix 3).
A case may carry "value" (a resolved expression) instead of "fn"/"args".
Sign convention: expense budgets and actuals are NEGATIVE, income POSITIVE. The
sole exception is §4.5A's pool, whose figures are positive magnitudes and whose
`unassigned` alone may be negative.
Two round-04 integration corrections are pinned here rather than only described:
an ARCHIVED CATEGORY keeps its bxCatTotals entry but contributes nothing to
bxHeaderTotals (§3.9, "excluded from every total"), and bxProgress clamps
`over_fraction` to [0,1] while leaving `over_ratio` uncapped (spec Addendum 5).

legacy_compare._why: Legacy scores every matching category as exactly 1 and max() returns the first inserted, so it answers sub-aaa-fuel on the strength of the single word MIDRAND. bxSuggest matches WOOLWORTHS, FOOD and MIDRAND against sub-bbb-groceries for a score of 3. Note that sub-aaa-fuel also sorts FIRST by id, so the id tiebreak would give the legacy answer too — only the count-based score reaches the right one.

The index was built from 'Vida e Caffe Rosebank'. The legacy match is case-sensitive so it returns None; bxSuggest lowercases both sides and scores 2 (vida, caffe — the one-letter 'e' is below the length-3 floor).
